title: Top-account temporal credit wallet and rollback policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Strategic customers frequently request time-boxed roadmap commitments. Current intake patterns rely on manual PM/AE negotiation and ad-hoc sprint reservations which causes: unpredictable engineering load, opaque promise accounting, and difficulty enforcing rollbacks when scope is deprioritized.

Goal: Implement a temporal "credit wallet" that allocates redeemable roadmap credits to qualifying top accounts. Credits represent negotiable, expiring reservation currency that can be consumed for scoped, timeboxed deliverables (e.g., bugfix slot, integration work, product tweak). The system will provide automated bookkeeping, visibility to CS/AE/PM, and a rollback/recapture policy to reclaim credits when commitments are not used or when deliverables are deprioritized.

Success metrics:
- 90% reduction in manual spreadsheet intake work across PM/CS for prioritized asks within Q following launch.
- <5% unaccounted-for credit discrepancies between ledger and delivery dashboard.
- Customer satisfaction (NPS post-delivery) for work delivered from credits >= baseline.
- Measurable decrease in surprise scope on sprint planning (tracked via planning rework metric).

Scope:
In scope: credit issuance rules, expiration windows, UI for CS/AE to view wallet balance, PM-facing allocation/approve flow, automated ledger, integration with roadmap scheduler for token reservation, rollback/recapture flow and audit logs.
Out of scope for MVP: billing integration (chargebacks), cross-account credit transfers, legal contract language.

Approach overview:
1) Rules engine (PM-configurable policies) to qualify accounts, set credit amounts, and expiration windows.
2) Wallet UI in Console for account advocates to request reservations and see balance.
3) Reservation endpoint that creates a short-lived roadmap hold and generates audit entries.
4) Automatic rollback: when a reservation expires or delivery is canceled, credits return to wallet and an audit record plus customer notification is generated.
5) Reporting: ledger reconciliation dashboard and weekly anomaly alerts.

Tradeoffs / risks:
- Risk of increased operational complexity for CS/AE workflows; mitigate by progressive rollout with training and guardrails.
- Potential for perceived unfairness if credit amounts/qualification are opaque; mitigate with transparency docs and an appeals path.
- Engineering capacity hit for scheduler integration; propose a lightweight MVP hold mechanism before deep integration.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (MVP internal pilot) — 6 weeks: implement wallet UI, rules engine stub, reservation endpoint using MVP scheduler hold, audit logs, and reconciliation job. Pilot with 3 strategic accounts.
Phase 2 — 4 weeks: iterate on UX, add expiration email notifications, anomaly alerts, and open pilot to CS team.
Phase 3 — 6 weeks: broader release + integrations (billing & contract language) and automation for acceptance criteria evaluation.

Compliance & security notes: audit trail required for enterprise customers; storage of wallet metadata in customer-managed tables for Private deployments is a future requirement.

Related artifacts: Confluence PRD (link below), design mockups, prototype GitHub branch and dashboard prototype.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CS/AE can view a customer's current credit balance and expiration metadata from the Console.
2) PM can allocate credits via a deny/approve flow; approvals create ledger entries.
3) Reservation API creates a scheduler hold and returns reservation id; reservation automatically expires per policy and credits are returned.
4) Audit log records issuance, reservation, consumption, rollback with timestamps and actor ids.
5) Admin dashboard reconciles ledger totals with reservation records within a 24h reconciliation window.
6) Pilot with 3 customers successfully issues, consumes, and rolls back credits without manual ledger fixes.
